reason: Reproduced end to end, twice, with a pageerror listener attached before driving. render-b.js:688 is verbatim `focus: function () { event.currentTarget.focus({ preventScroll: true }); }`; currentTarget is nulled when dispatch ends, so every stepper history entry stores a closure that throws. Driven at ?state=owner-editing on master.html (which loads render-b.js as an external script, so this is the live code, not a stale part file): click 'Move a week later', then press the visible .b-undoAct - 'Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'focus')' fires on EVERY undo, at 390x844 and at 1440x960, and on the Ctrl+Z path too. Both consequences the finding claims are measured. (1) Focus: paintUndo() disables .b-undoAct before top.focus() runs, so the focused control is disabled and focus falls to the body - measured activeElement = BODY at both 390 and 1440 after the button path. (2) Place: undo() lines 532-541 has no try, so the throw at line 540 makes line 541 `window.scrollTo(0, top.at)` unreachable. At 390 scrollY was 400 before the press, 899 after the stepper click, and 769 after undo - not restored to the remembered 400 (the finding said 793; the exact figure differs by a repaint, the substance does not). The comment at line 525-526 says this restore exists precisely because 'Undo used to restore the moment and leave them a screen away from it' - the regression it was written to prevent is back, now behind an exception. The gate claim is also correct. interaction-check.mjs:468 'undo returns focus to the control that made the change' only exercises Ctrl+Z, where the .b-step was clicked immediately before and never lost focus - I confirmed activeElement stays .b-step there even though the closure still throws, so the assertion is satisfied without anything being restored. The gate cannot see the exception either: pageErrors is asserted once, at line 77, before any interaction block runs, and never again - so an uncaught TypeError raised at line ~456 is collected and discarded. Not restating the gates, not taste, no constraint touched, no colour or weight involved. A hard uncaught exception on the single most frequent undo in the product's only reversibility surface, annihilating both focus and place, is disqualifying at 9.5.
sharpenedFix: Take the proposed fix and widen it one notch, because the stepper is not the only entry that strands focus. (1) In step()'s click handler (render-b.js:677) capture the node: `var pressed = event.currentTarget;` as the first line, then `focus: function () { if (pressed && pressed.isConnected) pressed.focus({ preventScroll: true }); }`. (2) In undo() make the scroll restore unstrandable: `try { if (top.focus) top.focus(); } finally { if (typeof top.at === 'number') window.scrollTo(0, top.at); }`. (3) Add the general case the finding stops short of: focus: is the ONLY such closure in the file (grep confirms one other `focus:` at 1369 is an input handler, not a history entry), so every non-stepper undo - visibility toggle, rename, delete - has no focus restore at all. Driven: toggle Hidden, press the Undo button, activeElement = BODY, no exception, no restore. So in undo(), before paintUndo(), record `var hadFocus = document.activeElement === root.querySelector('.b-undoAct')`, and after paintUndo, if the entry supplied no focus closure and hadFocus is true and the control is now disabled, park focus on the editor panel or the affected .b-grab rather than letting it fall to the body. (4) Harden the gate so this cannot pass again: move (or repeat) the 'zero console errors' assertion to AFTER the interaction blocks so a throw raised during driving is actually asserted, and change the assertion at interaction-check.mjs:468 to exercise the .b-undoAct path with a non-zero scrollY, asserting both activeElement.classList.contains('b-step') and window.scrollY back at the remembered value.
